name: Galaxy
line: The cancer network as a navigable galaxy: a 3D force layout flattened into a disc, drawn as glowing stars (IARC group colours for exposures, white for cancer types) in perspective with depth fade, turning slowly until touched; drag (or swipe sideways on a phone, or the turn buttons) to rotate, and the signature moment is the camera flight into Tobacco smoking, then Lung cancer, then back out to the whole sky for the lesson.
notes: Pure canvas 2D, no libraries; the 3D layout is computed once on load (about a tenth of a second). On touch, the canvas keeps vertical page scrolling (touch-action: pan-y) and uses only sideways swipes to turn, so the page is never hijacked; the turn-left, turn-right and pause buttons work everywhere. The slow rotation stops on the first drag or turn, can be resumed with the play button, and never starts with reduced motion (flights are then instant). Selecting a star from the search, the map or the entry card flies the camera to it. On phones the sky is masked above its own area so text never sits on stars. Sora is Latin-only (no Cyrillic). Without JavaScript the explorer's network drawing is shown in starlight.
